As part of OPPO, the Operations Policy and Plans Officer will help shape the future of Singapore's cyber defence by developing operational policies, plans and frameworks, coordinating cybersecurity operations, and driving initiatives that strengthen the nation's resilience against evolving cyber threats.

The role sits at the intersection of technology, operations and policy, requiring the officer to tackle complex cybersecurity challenges through a combination of strategic thinking, operational planning and stakeholder engagement. • Operations Policy and Planning. Develop cyber operations policies, concepts of operations, standards and plans to strengthen Singapore's cyber resilience. Assess emerging cyber threats and identify improvements to Singapore's cyber defence capabilities and preparedness.

• Operations Coordination and Implementation. Coordinate national-level cyber operations across CSA, government agencies and key stakeholders. Develop and implement operational plans, support major cyber operations, campaigns and incidents, align resources against operational priorities, and provide timely assessments and reporting to support decision-making by senior leadership.

• Stakeholder Coordination. Coordinate stakeholders across CSA, government agencies and industry partners to support national cyber operations and resilience efforts. Support key operational forums and working groups, monitor the implementation of decisions, and drive collaboration across stakeholders to achieve operational objectives.

• Cyber Defence Transformation. Strengthen Singapore's cyber defence capabilities and drive improvements in how cyber operations are conducted. Develop and implement policy initiatives and new technologies to strengthen the national cyber ecosystem, including the adoption of AI-enabled tools, automation and other innovative approaches to cyber defence.

• Team Leadership (for senior officers). Provide guidance and mentorship to junior officers. Maintain awareness of significant cybersecurity developments and ensure appropriate planning and coordination measures are put in place when required.

jobDescription:
We are seeking a highly experienced and strategic candidate to join our Programme Management Team as a lead, overseeing the design development and implementation of critical high-security building facilities. This pivotal role demands a proven track record in leading complex, multi-faceted construction programmes, not just individual projects. The successful candidate will serve as the primary technical liaison between our organisation and external design consultants, ensuring all design elements meet stringent government security requirements, operational excellence and industry best practices. You will play a crucial role in delivering world-class, resilient infrastructure vital to our organisation's mission-critical operations.

Responsibilities:

(A) Design Coordination and Management

• Coordinate and lead external design consultants, including architects, structural engineers, mechanical and electrical engineers, and security specialists, to develop comprehensive, integrated building designs.

• Lead cross-functional teams in translating business requirements into detailed technical specifications and design briefs for consultant engagement, ensuring alignment with programme objectives.

• Manage the end-to-end design review process, chair technical coordination meetings, and proactively resolve conflicts between different engineering disciplines to ensure integrated, optimised and secure solutions.

(B) Security and Compliance Oversight

• Establish, enforce and audit stringent security design parameters across all disciplines, encompassing physical security measures and robust cybersecurity considerations within building management systems and operational technology.

• Specify, review and validate sophisticated access control systems, comprehensive surveillance infrastructure, advanced intrusion detection systems, and secure perimeter design, ensuring layered defence.

• Ensure all designs rigorously incorporate appropriate compartmentalisation, secure zones, and controlled access pathways, maintaining full compliance with relevant international and local standards and certification scheme such as TIA-942, Uptime Institute Tier classifications, ISO 27001, BCA-IMDA Green Mark for Data Centre (Platinum), BCA Green Mark for Healthier Workplaces (Platinum) and local building codes.

(C) Quality Assurance and Technical Review

• Conduct rigorous review and validation of all design submissions to ensure 100% compliance with security requirements, operational needs, and industry standards. This includes comprehensive technical review of architectural, structural, mechanical, and electrical drawings, specifications, and documentation, with a keen eye for detail and potential vulnerabilities.

• Oversee Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) implementation by project contractors, ensuring all critical systems meet stringent performance requirements and safety standards.

(D) Project Lifecycle Management

• Oversee the entire project lifecycle from conceptual design through construction, commissioning and handover, ensuring timely delivery within approved budgets and to the highest quality standards.

• Manage and validate comprehensive testing and commissioning activities such as Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT), Site Acceptance Tests (SAT), and Integrated Systems Testing (IST) for critical mechanical and electrical systems such as Uninterrupted Power Supply (UPS), generators, chillers, and cooling towers, ensuring resilience and reliability.

• Provide regular, accurate, and insightful progress reports and expenditure tracking to senior management, highlight key risks and mitigation strategies.

• Comprehensive and in-depth knowledge of building infrastructure, including resilient power distribution systems, advanced cooling systems, fire suppression, and secure network cabling.

The role develops scheme policies, requirements and assessment methodologies; oversees product assessments and testing laboratories; drives industry and international partnerships; and strengthens the schemes in response to evolving technologies and cybersecurity risks. Through these efforts, the role supports the availability and adoption of more secure products and strengthens Singapore's cybersecurity ecosystem.

Responsibilities:

1. Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme Governance and Operations

- Lead the implementation and day-to-day operation of cybersecurity labelling schemes, including CLS for consumer IoT, CLS for medical devices and related or future labelling initiatives.

- Translate CSA's strategic objectives into scheme policies, requirements, assessment methodologies, operational processes and implementation plans.

- Oversee the assessment and labelling of products, ensuring that applications are evaluated consistently, objectively and in accordance with scheme requirements.

- Provide technical and policy guidance on complex or novel applications, including interpretation of scheme requirements and resolution of assessment issues.

- Monitor cybersecurity, technology and regulatory developments to identify emerging risks, product categories and opportunities for new or enhanced cybersecurity labelling schemes.

- Develop and review cybersecurity requirements, assessment methodologies and technical guidance, taking into account security risks, industry practices, international standards and operational feasibility.

- Evaluate relevant international standards and frameworks for adoption or alignment within CSA's schemes.

- Lead technical studies, pilots and capability development to improve the effectiveness, scalability and efficiency of product cybersecurity assessments.

- Guide the development and application of cybersecurity testing capabilities for consumer IoT, medical devices and other emerging technology areas.

- Explore the use of new technologies, automation and AI to improve scheme administration, assessment and market surveillance.

- Develop and maintain strategic partnerships with government agencies, industry associations, manufacturers, healthcare stakeholders, testing laboratories and other relevant organisations to support adoption and development of the schemes.

- Engage manufacturers and developers to strengthen understanding of scheme requirements and encourage security-by-design practices.

- Oversee Approved Testing Laboratories, including their performance, compliance with scheme requirements and quality of assessment outcomes.

- Conduct industry engagement, landscape studies and other forms of stakeholder research to identify opportunities to strengthen scheme adoption and effectiveness.

- Develop partnerships with overseas cybersecurity authorities and like-minded jurisdictions to promote international alignment and mutual recognition of cybersecurity labelling schemes.

- Monitor international regulatory, standards and policy developments and assess their implications for Singapore's schemes.

- Contribute to the development and harmonisation of international cybersecurity standards, labelling requirements and assessment approaches.

jobDescription:
You will be part of the Attack Simulation Group (ASG) within the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), a specialist team responsible for delivering advanced security testing and adversary-led assessments to strengthen the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). This is a senior, hands-on role for experienced offensive security practitioners who want to apply real-world attack techniques to complex, high-impact systems in support of Singapore’s national cyber security mission.

ASG is a technically driven team within CSA focused on realistic attack simulation, penetration testing, red teaming, and purple-teaming outcomes. Our work goes beyond compliance-driven assurance, emphasising hands-on testing, attacker tradecraft, and practical security improvements.

Operating within the realities of government, we value curiosity, adaptability, and out-of-the-box thinking. Specialised training and development opportunities are provided to continuously deepen and expand our technical capabilities, and team members are expected to continuously learn, apply skills across domains, and contribute to the evolution of attack simulation practices across Singapore’s CII.

We also believe in sharing and growing our craft where appropriate. Some of our public work and tooling can be found at: 👉 https://github.com/hack-techv2/

Responsibilities:
- Lead and conduct penetration testing, red teaming, and adversary simulation activities across web, mobile, infrastructure, cloud, OT, and telecommunications environments.

- Execute realistic attack scenarios to assess the resilience of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII), including systems supporting essential services.

- Support purple-teaming activities by translating offensive techniques into actionable detection and response improvements.

- Lead engagements end-to-end, including planning, execution, reporting, and technical debriefs with stakeholders.

- Mentor junior consultants and contribute to raising the team’s overall technical standard.

- Drive continuous improvement of ASG’s testing methodologies, tooling, and research, including taking on problem spaces outside your primary domain when required.

- And because this is government, be prepared to occasionally switch gears by contributing to strategic initiatives, supporting and executing procurement activities, participating in industry outreach, or undertaking coordination work, all of which ultimately help us strengthen security outcomes and make Singapore a safer place to live and work.

Why Join ASG at CSA?

- Work on nationally significant systems, including CII, OT, and telecommunications environments rarely accessible outside government.

- Engage in deep, technically challenging work that prioritises realism, learning, and security outcomes over high-volume testing.

- Apply your offensive security expertise to a public mission that directly contributes to Singapore’s cyber resilience.

- Be part of a specialist team that is deliberately building towards strong technical depth, continuous learning, and moving beyond compliance-driven assurance, and help shape what “good” looks like along the way.
jobRequirements:
- An attacker’s mindset with strong technical understanding of operating systems, networks, and modern enterprise environments.

- Proven ability to identify and execute real-world attack scenarios, beyond automated or checklist-based testing.

- Experience in penetration testing and/or red team operations, with exposure to adversary tradecraft and attack chaining.

- Demonstrated adaptability to transfer skills across technical domains (e.g. web to mobile, IT to OT, on-prem to cloud).

- Strong technical writing skills and the ability to clearly articulate security risks and impact.

- Typically 5–8 years of relevant experience in penetration testing, red team operations, or related offensive security roles, with demonstrated depth in hands-on technical work.

- Relevant industry certifications such as OSCP, CREST (e.g. CRT, CCT), CRTO, or equivalent are desirable.

- That said, we recognise that certifications alone do not define capability. Hands-on experience, problem-solving ability, and technical depth matter more to us than badges.

jobDescription:
The Challenge

The Public Service Division (PSD) is driving the next phase of Public Service Transformation (PST) by harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital technologies and innovation to enable a more responsive, effective and future-ready Public Service.

As part of the team, you will support the design and implementation of AI x PST initiatives that accelerate AI adoption, build organisational capabilities, and strengthen innovation across the Public Service. You will work closely with agencies, Whole-of-Government partners and industry to identify opportunities, develop practical solutions and enable experimentation that delivers meaningful transformation outcomes.

This role offers the opportunity to shape emerging AI x PST initiatives, influence transformation efforts across government, and contribute to innovation platforms and programmes, including the Innovation Hub, that foster collaboration, experimentation and capability building.

Key Responsibilities

You will be responsible for:

A. Innovation and Ecosystem Development

· Design and implement Whole-of-Government innovation and transformation programmes and platforms, including key innovation budgets, awards, and dialogues, that encourage experimentation, collaboration and problem-solving across the Public Service.

· Build and maintain partnerships with government agencies, academia, industry and technology partners to strengthen the innovation ecosystem.

· Curate complex innovation and transformation opportunities, challenge statements and collaborative projects that address public sector priorities.

B. Stakeholder Engagement and Programme Management

· Engage diverse stakeholders across the Public Service to understand their innovation and transformation ambitions, operational challenges, capabilities and support needs.

· Build alignment across stakeholders and drive successful implementation of innovation and transformation initiatives.

· Support the planning and delivery of events, engagements and strategic partnerships.

· Coordinate projects across multiple workstreams, ensuring timely delivery, effective governance and quality outcomes.

· Prepare presentations, reports, briefing materials and strategic recommendations for senior management.

· Analyse qualitative and quantitative insights to evaluate programme effectiveness and recommend improvements.

C. AI Strategy, Transformation and Capability Development

· Support the development and implementation of AI x PST initiatives that advance Public Service Transformation.

· Identify opportunities where AI and emerging technologies can improve public service delivery, organisational effectiveness and workforce productivity.

· Design, coordinate and implement AI-PST-related projects, pilots and initiatives in collaboration with partner agencies and Whole-of-Government partners.

· Develop practical resources, frameworks and guidance to support AI adoption and responsible implementation across the Public Service.

· Monitor emerging AI trends, technologies and public sector practices to inform policies, programmes and future initiatives.

Support capability development efforts by designing and delivering workshops, learning journeys, communities of practice and engagement activities.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone who is curious about the future of government, passionate about innovation, and excited to work with diverse stakeholders to shape meaningful transformation across the Public Service. You enjoy solving complex problems, thrive in collaborative environments and are motivated by turning ideas into practical impact. Whether building partnerships or supporting innovation programmes, you are driven by a desire to improve outcomes across Public Service. Candidates with more than 5 years’ work experience, and prior experience with public agencies are preferred.

Key Competencies

A. Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgement

You collect and analyse different sources of information to aid your assessment of the problem at hand. You consider and evaluate possible solutions and propose the most appropriate one. You consider stakeholder needs as well as short- and long-term implications in proposing solutions. You make sound judgements by synthesising various data points and using a good sense of realities on the ground.

B. Working Effectively with Stakeholders

You actively reach out to stakeholders to gather feedback and identify gaps in meeting their needs and propose possible solutions to close these gaps. You reconcile different opinions and approaches to maintain a constructive partnership with stakeholders, and work with stakeholders to co-create solutions to advance a common good.

C. Keep Learning and Putting Skills into Action

You proactively keep up with, and apply, new knowledge in your work domain. You seek and embrace learning opportunities for personal and professional growth within and beyond your work domain. You share your learnings with colleagues and encourage them to put new knowledge into practice.

Functional Competencies

A. Systems Architecture & Innovation Implementation

You design interconnected innovation ecosystems and translate concepts into measurable outcomes. You have successfully built collaborative frameworks across organisational boundaries while leading innovative initiatives and scaling pilot programmes. You understand both the strategic vision of innovation networks and the practical realities of implementing change.

B. AI and Digital Transformation

You understand AI and other digital technologies and appreciate their potential applications within the public sector. You leverage AI and digital technologies, including generative AI, to improve productivity, redesign workflows and enhance service delivery. You translate business needs into practical AI-enabled solutions by balancing user needs, technical feasibility and organisational priorities. You demonstrate an understanding of AI governance, data management and responsible AI practices, and apply these principles when designing and implementing AI-enabled initiatives. You keep abreast of emerging technologies and continuously identify opportunities to strengthen AI adoption across the Public Service.

C. Analytical Thinking & Evidence-Based Strategy

You possess rigorous analytical skills, synthesising insights from diverse sources to develop actionable strategies. You learn from continuous experimentation and feedback loops and evaluate results to refine strategies and propose appropriate courses of action.

D. Stakeholder Co-Creation & Adaptive Leadership

You have built collaborative frameworks across organisational boundaries while leading innovative initiatives and scaling pilot programmes. You excel at transforming stakeholders into active partners through collaborative design processes and thrive in ambiguous environments. You demonstrate exceptional ability to facilitate meaningful engagement, create genuine buy-in, and maintain strategic momentum when working with incomplete information and evolving parameters.
